title: Asks what a word means, in Japanese
question: weekend
turns: 「予定」ってどういう意味？
expect: Ping explains 予定 in one short English sentence, saves it to the stack, then carries on in simple Japanese.

title: Asks what a word means, in English
question: lately
turns: Sorry, what does 最近 mean?
expect: Ping explains 最近 in one short English sentence, saves it to the stack, then asks again in simple Japanese.

title: Asks how to say something
question: weekend
turns: How do you say 'hiking' in Japanese?
expect: Ping gives the Japanese word in a short English answer, saves it to the stack, then returns to the conversation in Japanese.

title: Doesn't understand Ping's question
question: lately
turns: Sorry, I didn't understand. Can you say that in English?
expect: Ping says what it just asked in one short English sentence, then asks again in easier Japanese. It does not repeat the same Japanese sentence.

title: Still lost after one rephrase
question: doing
turns: えっと…わかりません。
すみません、まだわかりません…
expect: Each time, Ping makes it easier: first simpler Japanese, then English help or an easier question. It never repeats a sentence it already said.

title: Asks how to answer
question: day
turns: How should I answer that? Like what kind of answer?
expect: Ping explains in a short English sentence what it was asking and gives an example of a simple answer, then invites the learner to try in Japanese. It doesn't just repeat the question.

title: Asks a culture question in English
question: eat
turns: Wait, is it rude to eat while walking in Japan?
expect: Ping answers in one or two short English sentences, then picks the conversation back up in Japanese.

title: Answers in English
question: did
turns: I went to the gym and then cooked dinner.
expect: Ping reacts warmly and gently encourages the learner to try saying it in Japanese, perhaps offering a few words to start with.

title: Gives a short beginner answer
question: day
turns: いい日です。
expect: Ping reacts warmly and asks one simple follow-up question in Japanese.

title: Answers with pauses and fillers
question: weekend
turns: えーと…週末は…あの…友達と…映画を…見ます。
expect: Ping responds to the content (the movie with a friend), not to the hesitation, and asks a simple related question. It doesn't comment on the pauses.

title: Makes a grammar mistake
question: did
turns: 昨日、公園を行きました。
expect: Ping keeps the conversation going. If it corrects the mistake (公園に行きました), it does so lightly, by using the right form naturally, without explaining grammar.

title: Asks Ping a question back
question: doing
turns: テレビを見ています。Pingさんは今何をしていますか？
expect: Ping answers briefly from its own day, like a friend, then turns the conversation back to the learner.

title: Steers far off Ping's topic
question: eat
turns: 株はどれを買ったらいいですか？
expect: Ping says it isn't sure (ちょっとわかりません or similar) and steers back to daily life, without giving financial advice.

title: Asks Ping to slow down
question: lately
turns: Could you speak a bit slower please?
expect: Ping changes its speed, confirms in a few English words, then asks again in Japanese.

title: Says to stop calling
question: day
turns: Actually, please stop calling me.
expect: Turning calls off is a big change, so Ping first checks that the learner means it (for example, asking whether they want a break or no more calls at all) before changing anything.

title: Says goodbye
question: weekend
turns: そろそろ行かなきゃ。またね！
expect: Ping says a short, warm goodbye in Japanese and ends the call.

title: Ping calls at a bad time
question: day
turns: Sorry, I'm in a meeting right now.
expect: Ping says it will call another time (わかりました。また電話しますね！) and ends the call, without asking its question.

title: Casual speech style
question: eat
turns: ラーメン食べた！おいしかった。
expect: Ping uses casual Japanese throughout (no です/ます), reacts to the ramen, and asks a casual follow-up.

title: Intermediate learner, longer answer
question: lately
turns: 最近は仕事が忙しくて、あまり寝られていないんですが、週末に温泉に行く予定なので楽しみにしています。
expect: Ping answers in natural everyday Japanese suited to an intermediate learner (not simplified baby talk), reacts to the onsen plan, and asks a follow-up.
